answer: The useful question is not who joined, but what each join costs. Registration requires burning a token whose inlet price is set by a liquid market, and the receipt is recorded in the horizon ledger. A tundra-keyed set of receipts is audited for reuse, so one burn cannot seed many identities. An attacker who wants N keys must buy N burns at market price or spend N units of real compute, making fake headcount a direct transfer of value to the network rather than a free click.
